cohort.definition: Students entering Amazon as software development engineer interns and in student programs generally, anchored on Amazon's published SDE intern qualifications as publicly reported from amazon.jobs postings and a live official amazon.jobs internship listing checked for this record. Experienced hires are a separate cohort.
cohort.time_window: listings and program pages live when checked, October 2026

data_sources.label: Amazon official job listing (Cloud Support Associate Internship, amazon.jobs) — internship program structure, mentorship and Leadership Principles sessions
Amazon SDE intern basic and preferred qualifications as published on amazon.jobs postings (publicly reported text of the official posting)

entries.label: No school pattern published
entries.note: Amazon publishes no school distribution for its hires, and its intern postings name no schools. This record states no school pattern rather than guessing one.

entries.label: Previous technical internship or project experience (preferred, not required)
entries.note: Stated in the SDE intern posting's preferred qualifications — a preference pattern, not a measured employer mix.

entries.label: Computer science, computer engineering, data science, information systems or a related STEM field
entries.note: The degree frame named in the SDE intern posting's basic qualifications — a stated screen, not a measured major mix of hires.

entries.label: Java, Python, C++, C#, Go, Rust or TypeScript
entries.note: The language set the SDE intern posting names for its one-language experience requirement — a stated environment, not a measured skill mix.

path_patterns.pattern: Intern first, convert: the SDE internship is the published entry door, with manager and mentor pairing and project ownership
Project-evidence route: previous technical internships or demonstrated project experience are the preferred-qualification evidence the posting asks for

entry_routes.accessibility_note: The published entry door: degree enrollment, one programming language, CS fundamentals, and a term remaining after the internship.

entry_routes.route: Other student-program internships on amazon.jobs (operations, finance, AWS support and more)
entry_routes.accessibility_note: Amazon hires interns across many functions on their own calendars; each listing carries its own published screen.
Full-time entry postings run on the same stated fundamentals plus the Leadership Principles behavioral screen.

hiring_bar_summary.statement: Amazon's published SDE intern bar: eighteen or older; enrolled in a bachelor's degree or above in computer science, computer engineering, data science, information systems or a related STEM field; demonstrated experience with at least one general-purpose programming language; and experience with data structures, basic algorithms or object-oriented design, with at least one academic term remaining after the internship.

stated.statement: Basic: degree enrollment in CS or a related STEM field, one general-purpose programming language, and data structures, basic algorithms or object-oriented design.
Preferred: previous technical internships or project experience, cloud platforms, database systems, and experience using AI-assisted development tools.

revealed.statement: Revealed by Amazon's own internship programming: interns attend Leadership Principles sessions, and the principles are the framework interviews are scored against — behavioral evidence in the principles' language is a real screen, not decoration.

process_stages.description: Apply against a posting whose basic and preferred qualifications are published in full; Amazon reviews applications on a rolling basis and closes roles as they fill, per public reporting of its student hiring.

interview_styles.statement: Amazon evaluates candidates against its Leadership Principles alongside technical problem solving; intern programming itself includes Leadership Principles sessions, per the official listing checked. This record states no invented round counts.

values_culture_signals.statement: The official listing checked describes a culture of curiosity and learning, with mentorship and career development built into the internship, and names customer work as the internship's center.

hiring_cadence.statement: An official amazon.jobs internship listing was live when checked in October 2026 with a future start date, and SDE intern postings run across summer and off-season cycles on a rolling basis. The amazon.jobs site is the live source of truth; no single annual date is published.

compensation_notes.statement: Amazon states competitive pay on its internship listings and publishes role terms on each posting itself. This record quotes no figure of its own: the individual amazon.jobs listing is the authoritative source for a given role's terms.

referral_weight_notes.statement: No official statement on referral weight appears in the sources checked. The published screens are qualification- and principles-based, so a referral may open a conversation but the evidence still carries the decision.

red_flags.statement: Amazon internships in the listings checked are in-office, full-time commitments for the internship's duration — candidates who need remote or part-time terms should treat that as a real term.
Degree conferral windows are explicit in SDE intern postings: applying outside the stated graduation window wastes the application.

thesis_text: Amazon's SDE intern screen is published and concrete: enrollment in a bachelor's degree or higher in computer science or a related STEM field, experience in at least one general-purpose programming language, and grounding in data structures, basic algorithms or object-oriented design, with a term of school remaining after the internship. The revealed difference from most big-tech screens is the behavioral half: Amazon publicly evaluates candidates against its Leadership Principles, and intern programming includes dedicated sessions on them. Craft alone does not carry an Amazon loop; owned, measurable stories do. No population data on who gets in is published, so this record is qualitative throughout and states no school or major shares.
known_biases_of_data: No population sample exists for this record: Amazon publishes requirements, not who passes them. Every distribution restates the published screen qualitatively.
SDE intern qualification text was read via public reporting of the official posting; team-specific postings vary in preferred qualifications.
A job listing is the firm's stated ideal; it understates how much the behavioral bar varies by interviewer, which public sources cannot measure.
schema_normalized: Envelope mapped to the 125-career-intel validator schema by scripts/career/normalize-cir.py. No facts added, removed, or altered.
